xanthi: A city in Thrace, northeastern Greece.
xanthine: (chemistry) Any of a group of alkaloids that include caffeine, theophylline, and theobromine as well as the parent compound, a precursor of uric acid found in many organs of the body.
xavier: Any of various notable people with this name as given name or surname, especially Saint Francis Xavier, a Spanish Catholic saint and missionary (1506–1552).
xenon: The chemical element (symbol Xe) with an atomic number of 54. It is a colorless, odorless, unreactive noble gas, used notably in camera flash technology.
xenophobia: A fear, antipathy, or hatred of strangers or foreigners.
xhosa: (uncountable) The language of these people, a Bantu language related to Zulu.
xhtml: Initialism of w:Extensible Hypertext Markup Language, a reformulation of HTML as an XML application.
xiang: A Chinese language spoken mainly in Hunan province, China
xiangqi: Chinese chess; a board game similar to chess, invented and traditionally played in China.
xiaolongbao: (Chinese cuisine) A type of dumpling or steamed bun (baozi) associated with eastern China, particularly Nanxiang near Shanghai.
xinjiang: An Uyghur autonomous region of China, located in the sparsely populated northwest. Official name: Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region. Capital: Ürümqi.
xiongnu: (historical) An ancient nomadic-based people that formed a state or confederation north of the agriculture-based empire of the Han dynasty.
xor: The logic function exclusive OR (as opposed to inclusive OR), whose output is true only when exactly one of its inputs is true.
xylem: (botany) A vascular tissue in land plants primarily responsible for the distribution of water and minerals taken up by the roots; also the primary component of wood.
